newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee slips on import covering.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee slips on import covering.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee fell in early trade on Monday because of commercial demand for dollars, but recovered when banks began selling the greenback, dealers said.
At 0450 GMT, the rupee was at 58.48 to the dollar, after opening at 58.50 and falling to 58.54, they said.
"The rupee fell on import covering demand for dollars by a state bank," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The dollar, however, is not seen rising above 58.60 during the day because the market is flush with sellers, an American Express Bank dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by three-quarters of a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.4125 and 59.5925.
Overnight call money was at its opening level of 12.25 percent, after rising to 12.5, dealers said.
